question.text: A famous part of the army of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth were the Winged Hussars, an elite cavalry unit that lifted the Ottoman siege of this present-day European country's capital city of Vienna.
question.clue: This country's far-right Freedom Party was led by Jorg Haider (yerg "HI"-der).

swap.leadin: This dynasty converted the Schonbrunn (shurn-brun) Palace from a hunting lodge to the permanent imperial summer residence where Franz Joseph died.
swap.text: Name this dynasty that inbred so much they developed a namesake chin. Under this dynasty's Charles V, their empire stretched from Spain to Hungary.
swap.clue: The founder of this house gained significant parcels of land after his victory at the Battle of Marchfeld, and the death of a later member of this house served as the extinction of its non-Styrian branch.

question.leadin: His death and that of his wife Sophie prompted the July Crisis.
question.text: Name this heir to the Austro-Hungarian throne whose assassination in Sarajevo by Gavrilo Princip helped lead to the outbreak of World War I.
question.clue: His wife was never permitted in the royal carriage, as a condition of his marriage to the lower-class woman after he became heir apparent following the death of his cousin Rudolf and father Charles Louis.

swap.text: A Congress in this Austrian city attempted to create a "balance of power" in Europe after Napoleon's defeat.
swap.clue: This city, the seat of the Hapsburg monarchy, served as a dual capital with Budapest after an 1867 compromise with Hungary.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the 1814 and 1815 Congress of Vienna.
question.text: The Congress was chaired by this Austrian who pushed for the Carlsbad Decrees and was forced to resign in 1848.
question.clue: The Academic Legion forced this man's resignation during the Revolutions of 1848.

swap.leadin: The Pragmatic Sanction of 1713 was an edict issued by a monarch of this royal house.
swap.text: Name this European royal house whose strategic marriages and inbreeding led to a namesake "jaw". Maria Theresa was the only female ruler of this House of Austria.
swap.clue: Inbreeding devastated the genetics of this family, giving them a namesake "lip."

question.leadin: Members of this family were elected to the Holy Roman Emperorship continuously from 1493 to 1740.
question.text: Name this dynasty of central and western Europe, which split into Austrian and Spanish branches in 1556.
question.clue: In the 19th century, this family took the title "King of Lombardy-Venetia".

swap.text: Name this Austrian queen whose inheritance was justified by her father Charles VI's Pragmatic Sanction. Her accession was disputed in the War of Austrian Succession.
swap.clue: To govern compulsory peasant labor, this monarch issued the Robot Patent.

question.leadin: The heir to the throne of this empire died by suicide along with his mistress in the Mayerling incident.
question.text: Name this empire that Franz Ferdinand became heir to after Crown Prince Rudolf's death. This empire had been formed as a dual monarchy in the 1867 Ausgleich.
question.clue: This empire formed after the Ausgleich, which made Franz Joseph I its first emperor.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about self-identified enlightened despots.
swap.text: When asked his thoughts on the American Revolution, this Austrian ruler and enlightened despot replied, "Madam, it is my trade to be a King". This son of Maria Theresa liberalized the curriculum of the University of Vienna and abolished the Robot Patent.
swap.clue: This ruler sent generals Lacy and Laudon on a series of tactical maneuvers in one conflict that saw little actual fighting, the War of Bavarian Succession, and, in response to the peasants' revolt of Horea, abolished serfdom.

question.leadin: It began when the arrival of Wehrmacht troops met with ecstatic pro-German crowds in March, 1938, and was followed by Hitler's call for the Sudeten from Czechoslovakia.
question.text: Name this union between Austria and Germany which was prohibited by the Treaty of Versailles.
question.clue: This action ended the political career of Wilhelm Miklas, who served as president of the nation in which it occurred.

swap.leadin: Paul McCartney led a 30-superstar "Rockestra" during relief concerts for Cambodia at this politician's suggestion.
swap.text: Name this politician who was the target of an expose written by Alfred Worm for Profil magazine. This leader succeeded U Thant ("ooh tant") as United Nations Secretary General.
swap.clue: His service in the Kozara mountains involved a massacre of Yugoslavs, and he was also a senior lieutenant during the deportation of forty thousand Jews from Salonika.

question.text: To help reconstruct Portugal's social structure after the earthquake, a queen regent with this name founded the Casa Pia children's educational institution. A later Braganza queen of this name was similarly known as "The Educator."
question.answerHtml: Maria [or Maria the Pious; or Maria the Mad; or Dona Maria I; or Maria the Good Mother; or Dona Maria II]

swap.leadin: This Habsburg was the main ruler of the Austro-Hungarian Empire in its final form, only dying in 1916.
swap.text: Name this longtime monarch who oversaw the Compromise of 1867 and entered the Three Emperors' League, doing some stuff which basically led to World War I.
swap.clue: The Fundamental Articles of his minister of commerce and agriculture Albert Schaffle was denounced by German nationalists, and he appeared beside Alexander II in Berlin in 1873 in support of the Dreikaiserbund.

question.text: Problems in the Balkans eventually led to the assassination of this heir to the Hapsburg throne in Sarajevo in 1914.
question.clue: It's 1914. You are a Bosnian Serb and member of the Black Hand Gavrilo Princip, who will assassinate this Archduke and his wife Sophie, setting off a chain of events that will begin World War I.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about setbacks for the Austro-Hungarian royal family which presumably made Emperor Franz Joseph I a very sad man.
swap.text: The Black Hand plotted this incident, in which Gavrilo Princip murdered a visiting Archduke in Sarajevo. This event was a primary catalyst for World War I.
swap.answerHtml: assassination of Franz Ferdinand [accept answers including synonyms for assassination such as "murder," "shooting," etc.]
swap.clue: Centrally planned by a man known as "Apis," it may have been possible due to its central figure's morganatic marriage to Sophie Chotek, whose visibility was insisted upon.

question.leadin: This son of Leopold II was named commander-in-chief of the Austrian army in 1806.
question.text: Name this winner over Andre Massena at First Zurich. More famously, he became the first person to beat Napoleon in over a decade when he beat Napoleon at Aspern-Essling.

swap.leadin: Franziska Feifalik's elaborate hair care routine for this woman included a wash with egg yolk and cognac every two weeks to create her "crown braid."
swap.text: Name this woman who commissioned a palace named after Achilles on Corfu as a summer refuge after a family tragedy. This woman was assassinated in Geneva by the anarchist Luigi Lucheni ("loo-KAY-nee").
swap.answerHtml: Empress Elisabeth of Austria [accept Duchess Elisabeth Amalie Eugenie; accept Elisabeth of Bavaria; accept Sisi or Sissi]

question.leadin: After this event, Count Eduard Taaffe claimed that a man died "due to a rupture of an aneurism of the heart."
question.text: What event was a murder-suicide in which a man shot his lover, Mary Vetsera, and then killed himself while staying at a hunting lodge in the village that lends its name to this event?
question.clue: Ida von Ferenczy was drafted to break the news of this event to Empress Elizabeth.

swap.leadin: This agreement created separate parliaments for a country's Cisleithanian and Transleithanian regions.
swap.text: Name this 1867 compromise that was negotiated by Friedrich von Beust and signed by Franz Joseph I.
swap.clue: Friedrich Ferdinand von Beust ("boyst") supported this event in a failed attempt to exact his revenge over a defeat at Koniggratz.
